title: Expression in capture: control surface, techniques, grouping, rhythm and reading aids

entries.title: restructure the capture control surface
entries.description:
Re-arrange the capture screen's controls so that later entries have somewhere to put new ones. This entry adds NO new musical capability: when it lands, exactly the same things are possible as before, reachable from better places.

The problem: src/components/capture/CaptureScreen.tsx ends in a single flex-wrap row of ten controls (repeat stepper, x4, stack, space, barline, triplet, chord symbol, select, paste, delete) at line ~392. It already wraps on a phone, and three later entries need to add controls to it.

The principle to apply is: sort controls by WHAT THEY MODIFY, not by what looks similar. There are four distinct scopes already present in the screen, and each gets its own home.

1. CONTROLS THAT MODIFY THE NEXT FRET PRESS go in a new thin latch strip across the top of the Fretboard component (src/components/capture/Fretboard.tsx). Move the existing `stack` toggle into it. A modifier for the next note belongs adjacent to where notes come from, not in a row of verbs, and it is where the user's thumb already is. Latches in this strip must be visibly lit while armed -- the existing `stack` button's primary/secondary variant treatment is the precedent, and the status line that reads "stacking onto the marked column" must keep working. Later entries add hammer-on / pull-off / slide latches to this strip; design it as a list so adding four more chips is data, not layout surgery.

2. CONTROLS THAT ACT ON THE COLUMN AT THE CURSOR keep the existing bottom toolbar. Make it contextual rather than uniformly disabled: `editable` (CaptureScreen.tsx:121) already computes that repeat, chord symbol and stack are meaningless on a barline, and the current code spends the screen space rendering them disabled at 30% opacity. Replace inapplicable controls with applicable ones instead of showing dead ones. This is where the row gets its headroom back.

3. CONTROLS THAT ACT ON A SELECTION already have a home: when a selection exists the row is replaced wholesale by copy / cut / delete / cancel (CaptureScreen.tsx:270). Do not change its behaviour; just confirm it still reads correctly after (2). A later entry adds group/ungroup here.

4. A NEW LONG-PRESS COLUMN INSPECTOR. Long-pressing a column in TabStaff opens a sheet for that column: the things you set while looking at a note rather than mid-riff. In THIS entry it hosts only what already exists -- the repeat count, the chord symbol, delete -- so it ships useful and is exercised by tests immediately. It is the extension point two later entries depend on (per-note decorations, duration), so its job is to be a general per-column property sheet, not a hardcoded three-control panel. Tapping a column must keep its current meaning (move the cursor there); the long press is additive and must not make a normal tap feel laggy or ambiguous. TabStaff is also rendered read-only in PlayView and SongView, so the long press must be opt-in via prop and absent where there is no `onSelectColumn`.

VERTICAL BUDGET. The screen is `h-dvh flex-col`: header, part chips, staff (`flex-1 min-h-0`), status row, optional chord form, controls row, fretboard. The new latch strip costs roughly 40px, which comes out of the staff's scroll area rather than the fretboard. This must be checked on a real phone viewport -- per docs/DECISIONS.md, "browser testing is part of done": look at it in Chrome at ACTUAL SIZE (not a magnified crop) in BOTH light and dark themes. The light theme is the one that has broken before.

TWO TRAPS DOCUMENTED IN THE REPO, both of which will cost hours if ignored. (a) If a style change appears to do nothing, the Turbopack CSS cache is stale: kill the dev server and use `npm run dev:clean`. Do not debug the CSS first. (b) Never express a visual tier as opacity over a surface token -- on the light theme `bg-raised` IS white and the tiers collapse. Name the colour per theme, as Fretboard.tsx now does.

DOES NOT DO, and who picks it up: no playing techniques of any kind (entry `playing-techniques`); no change to how tuplets are created or how many notes they can span (entry `generalised-grouping`); no note durations and no metronome (entry `rhythm-and-tempo`); no changes to the ASCII renderer or to src/lib/tab/layout.ts, because nothing new is being drawn.
entries.rationale: First because it is pure re-arrangement with no new data: it can be reviewed and verified in a browser on its own terms, and it creates the two extension points -- the fretboard latch strip and the column inspector -- that the techniques and rhythm entries both hang their controls on. Doing it after them would mean building those controls twice.

entries.title: playing techniques: hammer-ons, pull-offs, slides, taps and decorations
entries.description:
Make the techniques that are ALREADY IN THE SCHEMA capturable and visible. No migration is needed and none should be written.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS. src/lib/model.ts:52 declares `Technique` = palm_mute | dead_note | slide_up | slide_down | hammer_on | pull_off | bend | harmonic | vibrato | tap | let_ring. `techniques: TechniqueMap` (a per-string-index map to an array of techniques) is on `EventRow`, is listed in MERGEABLE_FIELDS (model.ts:208), is in the Drizzle schema (src/db/schema/domain.ts:238), is validated on the wire (src/lib/sync/protocol.ts:97), and is preserved by copy/paste (src/lib/local/clipboard.ts:90). Nothing writes it and nothing renders it. This entry is a renderer job plus a capture-UI job.

THE CENTRAL DESIGN DECISION, already made -- implement it, do not relitigate it. The enum contains two different kinds of thing:

- TRANSITIONS live BETWEEN two columns on one string: 5h7, 7p5, 5/7, 7\5. These are hammer_on, pull_off, slide_up, slide_down.
- DECORATIONS live ON a note: vibrato, harmonic, palm_mute, tap, let_ring, bend, dead_note (dead_note is already handled as the fret value "x" and needs nothing).

A transition is stored on the ARRIVING note, per string. `{"3": ["hammer_on"]}` on a column means "string 3 is reached by a hammer-on from the previous note on that string". The source note is derived from layout position and is NEVER stored as a `fromEventId`. That is deliberate: a pointer to another row is a second thing to merge and can dangle when the source column is deleted, whereas positional derivation means deleting the source simply reattaches the transition to whatever is now before it -- which is the right behaviour for a capture tool. Keeping this positional is also why no schema change is required.

RENDER IT ONCE, IN src/lib/tab/layout.ts. That module is the single source for both the on-screen staff and the ASCII serialiser, which is what makes it impossible for the export and the screen to disagree. Do not implement drawing in TabStaff and then again in ascii.ts.

- Decorations are cell affixes, produced in `cellText()`: 7~ vibrato, <7> harmonic, (7) let ring, 7b bend, a tap marked distinctly from a hammer-on. Column width already derives from the widest cell (layout.ts:132), so alignment comes free in both renderers.
- Transitions need a new per-string connector concept on `TabColumn` -- the glyph that occupies the gap BEFORE this column, per string. In src/lib/tab/ascii.ts, `staffRow` (line ~57) already appends exactly one RAIL character per gap per string row, so a connector is literally "emit h, p, / or \ instead of -". Choosing those four characters is not arbitrary: it makes the plain-text export look like the tab that bands already paste into chat, which is reason 2 in that file's own header comment.
- In src/components/tab/TabStaff.tsx, the connector is a thin sibling flex item (~1ch) between columns with one glyph per string row. It must line up with the staff rows exactly as the columns do, and must not break the chord row, the tuplet bracket row, the caret, or the barline rendering.

THE REPEAT WRINKLE, which must be decided explicitly and tested. A column with `repeat: 8` unrolls into eight layout columns from one event. A technique on that event therefore draws on every repetition. That is CORRECT for a repeated figure (5h7 5h7 5h7) and wrong for a single slide into a repeated figure; the escape hatch is that the user does not compress that column. Note that the chord row solves the analogous problem the other way, drawing only when `repetition === 0` (layout.ts:148) -- techniques deliberately do not. Add an ASCII test that pins this behaviour so the next person does not have to guess which way it went.

CAPTURE UI, using the two extension points the previous entry built.

- Transitions are LATCH CHIPS in the fretboard latch strip: h, p, slide-up, slide-down. Tap the chip, then tap the fret, and the chip DISARMS after one note -- unlike `stack`, which stays armed, because a three-note chord is common and a run of hammer-ons is not. Lit while armed, and the status line says what is armed. The four-second capture path (fret, fret, fret) must not get slower for someone who never touches a chip.
- Decorations are TOGGLES IN THE COLUMN INSPECTOR, per string, because you add vibrato while looking at the note, not mid-riff.
- `insertNote` in src/lib/local/editing.ts needs to accept techniques for the note being created; `stackNote` likewise for a stacked string.

PALM MUTE is the one notational exception: properly it is a span above the staff (P.M.------), the same machinery as `tupletSpans`. Do NOT build the span in this entry. Ship it as a per-note mark, which is enough for bass at practice, and say so in the spec so nobody mistakes it for an oversight.

VERIFY IN A BROWSER, per docs/DECISIONS.md: both themes, actual size, on a phone viewport. Connector glyphs at 11px JetBrains Mono are exactly the kind of thing that measures fine and reads as mush. Heed the `npm run dev:clean` and never-opacity-over-a-surface-token traps described in that file and the README.

DOES NOT DO: no bend target pitches (a bend renders as b, not 7b9); no palm-mute span row; no tuplet or grouping changes (entry `generalised-grouping`); no durations (entry `rhythm-and-tempo`); no parsing of techniques from pasted text (entry `ascii-import`, which depends on the characters this entry defines). MUST HANDLE, from the capture-control-surface review (specs/001-capture-control-surface/review.md, F14/FU1): the render-time prune at src/components/capture/CaptureScreen.tsx (near line 141) trusts `target`, and `target` is "no-column" while the cursor names a column the live query has not delivered yet. stack is the only latch that avoids setCursor(inserted.id), so any latch that stays armed across an insert would be dropped on every mid-part press. Fix this in that prune as part of adding the new latches, and test that a latch survives a mid-part insert.
entries.rationale: Second because it needs the latch strip and the column inspector from `capture-control-surface` to exist, and because the ASCII connector characters it chooses are the grammar the `ascii-import` entry later has to parse. It is independent of grouping, so either could come next, but techniques are the larger renderer change and benefit from landing while layout.ts is freshly in mind.

entries.title: generalised note grouping, not just triplets
entries.description:
Let a run of columns be grouped by any count, and let the group say whether it is a counted tuplet or plain phrasing. The data model is already general; the limitation is entirely in the UI.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS. `tupletId` and `tupletCount` are on EventRow and in MERGEABLE_FIELDS; the wire schema already accepts a count of 2..16 (src/lib/sync/protocol.ts:103); `groupAsTuplet(events, count)` in src/lib/local/editing.ts:482 already takes any count; `ungroupTuplet` exists at editing.ts:498 AND IS WIRED TO NOTHING; `tupletSpans` (src/lib/tab/layout.ts) turns shared ids into index ranges; and both renderers already draw the bracket with the span's count. What is hardcoded is one capture button that groups the last three playable columns, and a 3 baked into the SVG path of `TripletGlyph` in src/components/icons/index.tsx.

TWO KINDS OF GROUP, which is the one genuine modelling decision here. A TUPLET is three in the time of two: the number is load-bearing and must be drawn. A BEAT GROUP ("these four are one beat of sixteenths") is a reading aid, and printing 4 over four sixteenths is noise -- four in the time of four is just music. This app has no time signature and no beat grid: barlines are explicit stored events and durations are advisory, so most of what a user wants from "group these four" is visual phrasing rather than arithmetic.

So: ONE mechanism, TWO presentations. Keep the span-over-columns model exactly as it is and add one nullable field distinguishing a counted tuplet from a plain group. That costs a Drizzle migration, one line in src/db/schema/assert-model.ts (which fails `npm run typecheck` if the SQL schema drifts from model.ts -- it is a guard, not an obstacle, and the drift it reports is real), one entry in the wire schema, and one entry in MERGEABLE_FIELDS. Name it so a reader can tell the two apart without the docs. Render a counted tuplet with its number as today, and a plain group as a bracket with no number, in BOTH src/lib/tab/ascii.ts (`tupletRow`, which currently centres the label in a ,--3--, bracket) and src/components/tab/TabStaff.tsx.

THE UI CHANGE THAT MATTERS: grouping should act on the SELECTION. Tap-to-extend selection already exists and already drives copy / cut / delete from its own toolbar (src/components/capture/CaptureScreen.tsx:270). "Select six columns, group them" needs no count picker, no stepper and no hold-to-choose gesture, because the selection length IS the count. Put group and ungroup in that selection toolbar. Keep a one-tap "group the last three" for the common triplet in the main toolbar, since that is the case that happens mid-flow -- `tripletFromTail` in editing.ts already does exactly this and should be kept rather than removed. Wire `ungroupTuplet` up for the first time: ungrouping must be reachable both from a selection that overlaps a group and from a column that sits inside one (via the column inspector built in `capture-control-surface`).

The triplet glyph can no longer hardcode a 3. Either parameterise the numeral or let the button that means "last three" keep the literal glyph while the general control renders its own count -- decide, and say which in the spec.

EDGE CASES TO PIN WITH TESTS: a selection containing a barline (`groupAsTuplet` already filters barlines out -- confirm the resulting span is still contiguous and the bracket does not straddle the bar); a selection of fewer than two playable columns (currently returns undefined -- the UI must not offer the action); grouping columns that are already in a different group; a group whose columns include a `repeat: 8` column, which unrolls into eight layout columns inside one span.

VERIFY IN A BROWSER in both themes at actual size, per docs/DECISIONS.md. The bracket is a 0.3rem border-topped div at text-faint; a plain unnumbered bracket is a subtler thing than a numbered one and is exactly the sort of detail that disappears in the light theme.

DOES NOT DO: no durations and no metronome (entry `rhythm-and-tempo`), even though grouping and duration are both rhythm; no playing techniques (entry `playing-techniques`); no parsing of groups from pasted text (entry `ascii-import`).
entries.rationale: Third because it needs the column inspector from `capture-control-surface` as the place ungroup lives for a column inside a group, and because its bracket output is part of the text grammar `ascii-import` must parse. It touches layout.ts and ascii.ts, so it follows `playing-techniques` rather than racing it for the same files.

entries.title: import ASCII tab by pasting text
entries.description:
Parse ASCII tab back into parts, so a riff that already exists as text does not have to be re-entered with thumbs. This is the highest-value capability the app is missing: bands already have tabs in chat and on the web, and today the only way in is tapping.

The specification is already written, twice over. src/lib/tab/ascii.ts emits the format, and src/lib/tab/__tests__/ascii.test.ts is roughly 284 lines of exact-string examples of every shape the parser has to accept. Build the inverse of `toAscii`, and make the round-trip property the backbone of the test suite: for every fixture in that file, parsing the rendered text must reproduce the events it was rendered from. A round-trip test is worth more here than any number of hand-written parser cases, and it is free.

WHAT IT MUST ACCEPT, at minimum -- everything this app itself emits:
- the staff rows with their string labels and the leading/trailing pipe of the body
- bare fret numbers including two-digit frets, and x for a dead note
- pipe barline columns, which become stored barline events and must preserve the bar numbering that the arrangement's fromBar/toBar depend on
- the compact-density repeat form 7x8, which becomes one event with `repeat: 8` rather than eight events
- the chord row above the staff, which becomes `chord` annotations anchored to the column beneath
- the tuplet / group bracket row (,--3--, and whatever the unnumbered group form turned out to be), which becomes a shared tupletId across the span
- the transition connectors and decoration affixes defined by the `playing-techniques` entry -- read that entry's spec and the committed code rather than guessing the characters

STRING COUNT AND TUNING. The staff's row labels give the string names, and string index 0 is the HIGHEST-pitched string -- the opposite of the usual convention, for the reason documented in the README (bass extensions go downward, so numbering from the top means adding a fifth string never renumbers notes already captured). A five-row paste into a four-string song, or labels that do not match the song's tuning, is the main failure mode: decide whether to offer the closest matching tuning, create one, or refuse with a readable message, and say which in the spec. Do not silently drop a string.

TOLERANCE. Tab found in the wild is not this app's output: variable leading gutters, E| versus E space pipe, runs of rails of any length, trailing whitespace, blank lines between systems, multiple systems of the same part stacked vertically (which must concatenate, not become separate parts), and a line of lyrics or commentary in between. Be generous about whitespace and rails; be strict about anything that would silently produce wrong notes. When a line cannot be read, the import must say which line and why, and import nothing, rather than landing a half-parsed part -- a plausible-looking wrong tab is worse than a refusal.

ENTRY POINT: a paste-text target on the song screen that previews what was understood -- as the rendered staff, using the existing TabStaff -- before it commits. The preview is the honest check: it is the same renderer, so what you see is what will be stored. Create the events through the existing write path in src/lib/local/editing.ts so ids are UUIDv7, ranks are fractional index strings and every field gets its HLC; do not insert into Dexie directly, or the rows will not sync.

DOES NOT DO: no import of the arrangement line or of part letters/sections -- one paste makes one part's notes, and the arrangement stays hand-built; no MusicXML, no Guitar Pro files, no Songsterr scraping; no export changes, since `toAscii` already works.
entries.rationale: Fourth because it has to parse the text grammar that the two preceding entries define -- technique connectors and the group bracket forms -- and parsing a format that is still being extended means writing the parser twice. Everything it needs is in the repo by this point.

entries.title: durations, tap tempo and a click
entries.description:
Give the app a sense of time. Today `durationHint` is dead schema and `bpm` is decoration.

THE DEAD FIELD. `durationHint` (w | h | q | 8 | 16 | 32 | null) is on EventRow, in MERGEABLE_FIELDS, in the Drizzle schema, validated on the wire (src/lib/sync/protocol.ts:101) and carried by the clipboard -- and is written as `null` by all three insert paths in src/lib/local/editing.ts (lines ~290, ~359, ~452). It exists in nine files and does nothing. In a model this deliberate that is a liability: it reads as a supported feature to the next person who opens the file. This entry makes it real. (The alternative was deleting it; that decision has been made -- keep it, and wire it up.)

Its docstring says "advisory rhythm; null is valid and is the common case during fast capture", and that must stay true. Durations are optional, the positional column model remains primary, and nothing may require a duration to be set. A part with no durations at all must render and export exactly as it does today.

SET IT from a segmented row in the column inspector built by `capture-control-surface`: six fixed positions (w h q 8 16 32) that can be learned, rather than a dropdown that has to be read. This is the one place in the feature set where picking among values is genuinely the interaction, and it belongs where the user has already stopped playing. Consider also stamping the next note's duration from the fretboard latch strip if it does not crowd it -- optional, and say in the spec whether it was done.

TAP TEMPO. `song.bpm` is nullable and is rendered in PlayView's subtitle and nowhere else. Add tap tempo: tap in time a few times, average the intervals, round sensibly, write it to the song. Three taps and a division, and it answers the question everyone actually asks at practice ("what tempo was that?"). It must be reachable from capture without leaving the screen.

A CLICK, in PlayView. A metronome with a count-in turns that screen from a page you read into something you can play along with. Drive it from the song's bpm. Where durations and groups are present they should inform the click; where they are absent, a plain beat at the tempo is the correct and useful fallback -- do not make the metronome contingent on fully-notated rhythm, because that is the case this app is least likely to have. Use the Web Audio API and schedule ahead of time rather than relying on setInterval, which drifts audibly. Respect a silent/muted device and an autoplay policy that requires a user gesture before audio starts: the first tap on the start control IS that gesture, so start the AudioContext there.

THIS IS AN OFFLINE PWA. Whatever drives the click has to work with no network, which means no CDN audio library and no fetched samples -- synthesise the tick, or embed it. public/sw.js is hand-written and caches the app shell; read its header before adding anything that needs to be cached. Audio that works on the dev machine and silently fails on a phone in a rehearsal room with no signal is the specific failure to avoid.

PLAYBACK MUST NOT ASSUME A TIME SIGNATURE. There is none in the model. Bars are explicit barline events. A count-in is "four clicks at the tempo", not "one bar of 4/4".

DOES NOT DO: no pitched playback of the notes themselves -- this is a click, not a synthesiser, and the app is for reading tab while a human plays it; no time signature field; no per-part tempo (song-level only); no scrolling playhead through the tab (worth doing, but it is a reading feature and this entry is already large).
entries.rationale: Fifth because the duration control needs the column inspector from entry 1, because a click that honours groupings needs `generalised-grouping` to have landed, and because wiring durations before the grouping decision was made would have meant guessing how the two interact. Deliberately after `ascii-import` so the parser is not also chasing a duration row.

entries.title: note names, intervals, and seeing what a variant changed
entries.description:
Two read-side features that make a captured part easier to understand. Both are presentation over data that already exists, and neither writes anything new.

1. NOTE-NAME AND INTERVAL OVERLAY. A toggle on the tab staff that renders, instead of fret numbers, either the note names (A, C#) or the scale degrees / intervals relative to the chord in force. The hard parts are already built: src/lib/pitch.ts does MIDI and note arithmetic, src/lib/tunings.ts has `fretToMidi` and the fretboard geometry, and src/lib/chords.ts already parses chord symbols into notes and roles -- the Fretboard uses all of it to light up chord tones on the neck. This is the same computation pointed at the staff instead. It is how a player actually learns somebody else's riff: fret numbers say where to put a finger, note names say what the line is doing.

Where the toggle lives matters more than it sounds. It is a per-reader view preference, not song data, so it must not be stored as a synced field on the song -- it belongs in local view state (and may be remembered per device). It must apply to the staff in SongView and PlayView, and it must be honest in the ASCII export: either the export always uses fret numbers (the safe answer, since the exported text is what gets pasted into band chat and fret numbers are what tab means), or the export follows the toggle and says so on the page. Decide, and say which in the spec.

Column width is derived from the widest cell (src/lib/tab/layout.ts:132), and C# is wider than 7, so the staff will reflow when the toggle flips. Confirm that the chord row, the group bracket, the caret and the barlines all stay aligned, in both renderers if the export follows the toggle.

2. VARIANT DIFF. `variantOfPartId` is on PartRow (src/lib/model.ts) and is described as "set when this part is a variant of another -- A with a flourish". The arrangement layer uses `lastRepeatPartId` to play a variant on the final pass, and PlayView already substitutes it. But a variant is currently a silent full copy: nothing anywhere shows what is actually different about it, which means a reader has to compare two staves by eye, and a capturer has no way to confirm they changed only what they meant to.

Show a variant against its parent with the differing columns marked -- on the song page, and in the play view where the substituted pass is drawn. Diff the event sequences by content (frets, techniques, repeat, group membership, duration), not by id, because a variant made by copy/paste has entirely fresh ids (see `copyColumns` / `pasteClipboard` in src/lib/local/clipboard.ts, which deliberately mints new ids and fresh tuplet ids). Alignment matters: a variant that inserts one note should read as one inserted column, not as every column after it being different -- use a proper sequence alignment, and keep it fast enough to run on every part in a song in a `useLiveQuery` render path.

This is the app's own thesis applied to reading: a song is a short set of parts plus an arrangement, and "A x4 with a flourish on the 4th" is only compact if you can see what the flourish IS.

VERIFY IN A BROWSER in both themes at actual size, per docs/DECISIONS.md. A diff that distinguishes columns by colour alone has the exact problem the chord-tone work already hit and fixed: in the light theme the non-chord grey measured MORE contrasty than the accent, so the distinction rested entirely on hue at matched lightness -- the first thing to go in glare, on a stage, or for a colour-blind reader. Carry the distinction with weight or a mark as well as colour.

DOES NOT DO: no editing from the diff view (no "apply this change to the parent"); no diffing two arbitrary parts, only a variant against its declared parent; no transposition or capo features, even though the pitch machinery would allow them.
entries.rationale: Last because both features read data every earlier entry produces -- the overlay has to render technique affixes and the diff has to compare techniques, groups and durations -- so building either earlier would mean revisiting it after each later entry landed. Neither blocks anything, so this is also the natural place to stop if the roadmap is cut short.
